impact: Both defects still live in the current ticket bodies (verified 2026-08-02). T-014 can close with an oversized package: criterion 2's 'fails (or flags…)' disjunction contradicts the ticket's own 'deterministic checks are hard CI gates' ruling. T-022 can absorb the own-the-parsing spike inside the umbrella: Scope/In lists the spike while Intent and criterion 1 require it split into a child ticket first. Re-spec: T-014 criterion 2 = hard CI failure above 1 MB plus opening the platform-split revisit; T-022 = spike removed from Scope/In, umbrella limited to creating and linking child tickets when demand schedules a sub-item.
resolution: Fixed by the v0.2/v0.3 ticket re-spec applied 2026-08-02: T-014's package-size gate is now a mandatory CI criterion and T-022's spike-scope self-contradiction is fixed. The full verified requirements record is preserved in this issue's impact field.
title: T-014's package-size gate is optional, and T-022 contradicts itself on whether the spike is in scope
